subject.title: Agent lane lacks first-class scoped node exec path and stale nodes can hang or fail roughly

question: Should Codex app-server sessions expose a separate remote-node exec tool when the effective exec host remains `auto`/local, and what structured stale-node failure contract should that tool return?
rationale: Automation cannot safely decide whether to broaden model-visible remote shell access alongside native local shell, because that changes the operator-controlled remote-code-execution boundary and overlaps existing node approval and stale-node work.

options.title: Approve Explicit Mixed-Session Node Exec
options.body: Expose a pinned OpenClaw-owned node exec/process surface for configured nodes, require the existing approval binding, and return retryable structured unavailable results before timeouts feel like hangs.

options.title: Require Whole-Session Host Node
options.body: Keep `node_exec` visible only when the session's effective exec host is `node`, and document that mixed local-plus-node execution is not supported yet.

options.title: Defer To Node Tool Design
options.body: Route this through broader node-registered or node-hosted tool work instead of adding a generic shell surface now.

recommendation.title: Approve Explicit Mixed-Session Node Exec
recommendation.body: Expose a pinned OpenClaw-owned node exec/process surface for configured nodes, require the existing approval binding, and return retryable structured unavailable results before timeouts feel like hangs.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans the current Codex dynamic-tool path, gateway/node execution boundary, and security policy direction where steipete has the strongest recent routing signal.
